identity: Neutral gas-phase hydrazine H2N-NH2, CAS 302-01-2, singlet molecule with torsional/inversion motion; not liquid hydrazine, an ionic state, NH2NH radical or a chosen rigid planar conformer.
recommendation: Investigate a retained-thermal ATcT energy candidate and a separate NASA-thermal alternative, with torsion/inversion accounting as the central thermal check. A factor-two source disagreement alone does not prove the NASA thermal function is better.
science: The energy-aligned JANAF/NASA ratio rises from 1.499 at 1500 K to 2.263 at 4000 K, although their native atomization energies differ by only 85 J/mol. The large source difference is therefore thermal. ATcT lowers the JANAF physical atomization energy by 2.739 kJ/mol, giving a separate retained-thermal ratio 0.803 to 0.921. At 4000 K the molecular Cp differs by about 4.10 J/mol/K and entropy by 10.50 J/mol/K.
modern: The ATcT 1.228 gas-hydrazine page, including its 2026 computational-network inputs, was inspected. The 2017 primary formation-enthalpy study reports gas Hf 298=97.0+/-3.0 kJ/mol from isogyric reactions, consistent with the current ATcT97.69+/-0.29 value; its abstract was inspected, not the full calculation tables. The 2001 hydrazine thermodynamic survey is an identified optional resource for internal-motion ancestry. Its full text was not obtained, so no detailed torsion model is attributed to it here.
importance: Hydrazine belongs to reduced nitrogen chemistry and can matter in non-equilibrium nitrogen conversion. Its extremely low hot H-rich equilibrium share does not constrain production or storage in other environments.
conventions: Internal rotation/inversion and equivalent-well counting must be treated within one consistent molecular partition function. Do not add a conformer multiplicity or symmetry divisor to already evaluated NASA/JANAF entropy. The gas CAS record is separate from liquid hydrazine; no phase-change enthalpy is mistaken for gas atomization energy.
followup: A retained-thermal ATcT candidate is directly calculable. For a full thermal replacement, reconcile the evaluated torsional/inversion models and density of accessible states before selecting NASA or constructing a new function; then run fixed-network substitutions. DOI10.1021/je 000301o is useful optional ancestry, not a prerequisite for merging this numerical source review.
